findings.reason: §19 as written lands a link fix whose stated symptom (a non-null path in the code-context lookup) it does not produce, so the done-when "the code-context lookup renders a source path for a jt-60sa chunk" would be met only by also correcting the query the section never names.
findings.text: §19's central premise is incomplete: it says the code-context lookup "resolves `source_path` to null for them" and proposes to repair it by linking the orphaned jt-60sa `CodeChunk` rows, but the lookup's Cypher is `OPTIONAL MATCH (src)-[:HAS_CHUNK]->(node)` then `RETURN src.path AS source_path`, where `src` is the `CodeExample` (the only node type that carries an outbound `HAS_CHUNK` — schema `facility.yaml` and the chunk write at `imas_codex/ingestion/pipeline.py:522` both confirm it), and `CodeExample` has no `path` attribute (it carries `source_file`). So `source_path` is null whether or not the `HAS_CHUNK` edge exists, and every link the plan adds leaves the enrichment prompt still rendering an empty path. The string the prompt wants already has an owner — the denormalized `CodeChunk.source_file` (`imas_codex/schemas/facility.yaml:3288`), which §16 chose as the canonical source for `find_code` when it removed that function's CodeFile join — so the repair is to read `node.source_file` in `_build_code_context_query` (or `CodeFile.path` via `FROM_FILE`/`HAS_EXAMPLE`), extending the existing owner, rather than adding edges that the query never reads.

findings.reason: the section should drop the parallel-link-pass alternative and relink only by re-driving the existing writer, keeping one owner for the `HAS_CHUNK` edge.
findings.text: the section offers "a new link pass added beside the existing ones in `imas_codex/ingestion/graph.py` (`link_chunks_to_imas_paths`, `link_chunks_to_data_nodes`)" as a second way to relink the 201 existing chunks, but the `HAS_CHUNK` edge is written by the chunk write at `imas_codex/ingestion/pipeline.py:512-524`, and the two named `link_chunks_to_*` functions link chunks to IMAS paths and MDSplus data nodes — different targets from a CodeExample. A third link pass would be a second writer of an edge the pipeline already owns, in a module that owns neither the edge nor its source, which is the single-owner discipline §9 and §15 were landed to enforce. The path the plan already gives (re-ingest the 21 scored files, which re-drives the owning writer) achieves the same result with one writer.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — new behaviour lands as single owners rather than a spread of shallow wrappers: `resolve_remote_environment` (§6, one resolver passed down as parameters), `pending_embed_predicate` (§17, predicate rendered once for fetch/count/progress), `persist_data_access` (§9, the only DataAccess MERGE), `GraphClient.ensure_vector_indexes` (§15, the only CREATE VECTOR INDEX composer).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §19 attributes the null `source_path` on jt-60sa chunks to a missing `HAS_CHUNK` edge, but the code-context lookup reads `src.path` off the CodeExample (`imas_codex/discovery/signals/parallel.py:207`), a property the CodeExample schema does not carry; the source path is already owned by the denormalized `CodeChunk.source_file`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — week figures public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the two implementable sections add no surface — §14 reuses the pre-existing `--root` scoping option and the `--path-prefix` option added in §2, and §19 states "Interface budget: nothing added", pinning the behaviour with a test rather than a new view or option.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every mechanism the plan proposes cites the owner it extends: `resolve_service_url` for SLURM service discovery (§8/§10/§11), `ensure_vector_indexes` for vector-index DDL (§15), `check_tool`/`check_all_tools` for the environment probe (§6), the existing `WikiChunk-[:DOCUMENTS]->FacilitySignal` edge for the handbook link (§3), and the existing `--root` (paths) / `--path-prefix` (code) scoping options in §14/§19.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan declines parallel layers where it can: "no discover preflight command is added" (§6, extending `tools status`), the §6 review record shows `remote_environment` resolved in the facility-aware layer with the executor left facility-agnostic, and §19 states "never a hand-written MERGE or a fresh helper", preferring to reach the relink from the existing `ingest_files` call path.
